text:
Josh Kaul listed as keynote speaker at WISDOM immigration summit in Madison
J. B. Murphy
Attorney General Josh Kaul was listed as the keynote speaker at an immigration summit held by WISDOM, a group that describes itself as an interfaith network of affiliated organizations. The event took place on July 31 in Madison, according to information released on Aug. 19.
WISDOM’s stated goals include ending mass incarceration and closing prisons in Wisconsin. The group calls for state officials to commit to closing prisons and works toward advancing racial and economic justice, liberating people from the carceral system, ending perpetual punishment of directly impacted people, and shifting narratives that dehumanize individuals with conviction records. “Together, we work to end mass incarceration, expand funding to community-based alternatives to crimeless revocations and treatment alternatives and diversions. We will close prisons and re-invest money in programs that will rebuild communities that have been devastated by mass incarceration,” the group says on its website.
A video posted to WISDOM’s Facebook page features co-executive director remarks indicating the summit aimed to ensure “no one is terrorized by law enforcement.” Other organizers expressed concerns about sheriffs holding undocumented immigrants in jails and advocated for driver’s licenses for all residents regardless of immigration status.
Mark Rice, Wisconsin Transformational Justice Campaign Coordinator with WISDOM Wisconsin, outlined a demand for halting new prison construction and reducing the prison population through decarceration policies. Rice said to WKOW, “We’re calling on Governor Evers to start utilizing that power before he leaves office. It’s time for him to follow through.”
Governor Tony Evers reignited the commutation process in April after calls from groups including WISDOM. More than 800 inmates have applied for commutation since then.
